content.topic: Operability, outcomes and interventions for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH)

operability_and_patient_selection.summary: Eligibility for pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) decided by multidisciplinary CTEPH team; operability depends on diagnosis confirmation, surgical accessibility of chronic thrombotic obstructions, patient suitability, surgical team expertise, and resources. General criteria include pre-operative NYHA functional class and surgical accessibility of thrombi in main, lobar or segmental pulmonary arteries. Advanced age per se is not a contraindication. No single haemodynamic threshold or measure of RV dysfunction alone should preclude PEA.
operability_and_patient_selection.notes: Operability assessed by experienced surgeons, interventional radiologists/cardiologists, radiologists experienced in pulmonary vascular imaging, and clinicians with PH expertise.

additional_correlates_of_mortality: Additional cardiac procedures in operated patients
Comorbidities (coronary disease, left heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in not-operated patients)
registry_outcomes_and_predictors.hemodynamic_determinants_of_poor_prognos: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure (PAP) ≳ 38 mmHg and pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) ≳ 425 dyn·s·cm⁻5 reported as determinants of poor prognosis in survivors after surgical treatment

postoperative_management.ECMO: Post-operative ECMO recommended as standard of care in PEA centres; veno-arterial ECMO may be required for severe reperfusion oedema; persistent severe PH may be bridged to emergency lung transplantation with ECMO.
postoperative_management.follow_up: After PEA, follow-up in CTEPH centres to exclude persistent or recurrent PH; at least one haemodynamic assessment to be considered at 6–12 months after intervention.

balloon_pulmonary_angioplasty_BPA.indication: Effective treatment option for technically inoperable CTEPH; allows dilatation of obstructions down to subsegmental vessels inaccessible to surgery.
balloon_pulmonary_angioplasty_BPA.procedure_characteristics: Stepwise procedure requiring several (usually 4–10) separate sessions to engage under-perfused lung segments while limiting contrast and radiation per session.
balloon_pulmonary_angioplasty_BPA.technical_considerations: Navigation in distal pulmonary arteries requires particular expertise due to complexity and individual variability of pulmonary arterial tree.
balloon_pulmonary_angioplasty_BPA.bleeding_management: Bleeding usually resolves spontaneously but may require transient balloon inflation proximal to the site of bleeding to control it.

content.references_in_text: Multiple in-text citations noted (e.g., 461, 462, 465, 466) supporting registry data and recommendations.
